class.name: CaretWordBehavior
class.brief_description: Behavior of a caret when moving by words.
class.description: A resource for determining the caret behavior when moving by words. It allows configuration of how words, punctuation, brackets, and whitespace are broken down and used when moving between words. It is intended for use with [TextEdit] and [CodeEdit] but also has use in the [EditorSettings] to configure Godot Editor's script editor itself.

method.name: get_next_word_caret_left
method.description: Gets the next caret location to the left from the index [param start_column] in [param text_shaped] based on [param caret_word_behavior]. This also accounts for the flags [param is_newline] and [param is_remove].

method.name: get_next_word_caret_right
method.description: Gets the next caret location to the right from the index [param start_column] in [param text_shaped] based on [param caret_word_behavior]. This also accounts for the flags [param is_newline] and [param is_remove].

Custom behavior specified by the user.

Breaks are set around contiguous words. Words are considered their own token, separate from whitespace. [b]Note:[/b] Digits are included as 'words'. [b]Note:[/b] Non-word characters are considered whitespace by default.
For example: [code]example whitespace and "a string".[/code] will become: [code]|example| |whitespace| |and| "|a| |string|".|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Breaks are set around contiguous words as well as at the beginning of capital words.
For example: [code]var ExampleVariableName : int = 1 var example_variable_name : int = 1[/code] will become: [code]|var| |Example|Variable|Name| : |int| = |1| |var| |example_variable_name| : |int| = |1|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Breaks are set around contiguous words as well at the end of underscores within words.
For example: [code]var ExampleVariableName : int = 1 var example_variable_name : int = 1[/code] will become: [code]|var| |ExampleVariableName| : |int| = |1| |var| |example_|variable_|name| : |int| = |1|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Punctuation is considered as words. Breaks are set around contiguous words and punctuation.
For example: [code]example whitespace and "a string". func _process(delta : float) > void:[/code] will become: [code]|example| |whitespace| |and| |"a| |string".| |func| |_process(delta| |:| |float)| |>| |void:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Breaks are set around every instance of punctuation individually.
For example: [code]example whitespace and "a string". func _process(delta : float) > void:[/code] will become: [code]|example| |whitespace| |and| |"|a| |string|"|.| |func| |_process|(|delta| |:| |float|)| |-|>| |void|:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Punctuation is considered as a separate token. Breaks are set around contiguous punctuation.
For example: [code]example whitespace and "a string". func _process(delta : float) > void:[/code] will become: [code]|example| |whitespace| |and| |"|a| |string|".| |func| |_process|(|delta| |:| |float|)| |>| |void|:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Breaks are set around every instance of a bracket token.
For example: [code] ({}) {}word func _process(delta : float) > void:[/code] will become: [code]| |(|{|}|)| |{|}|word| |func| |_process|(|delta| : |float|)| > |void|:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Brackets are considered as a separate token. Breaks are set around contiguous brackets.
For example: [code] ({}) {}word func _process(delta : float) > void:[/code] will become: [code]| |({})| |{}|word| |func| |_process|(|delta| : |float|)| > |void|:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Bracket tokens will only have breaks if moving out of them.
For example: [code] ({--}) {--}word func _process(delta : float) -> void:[/code] when operating 'right' will become: [code]| ({--|}|)| {--|}|word| |func| |_process(|delta| : |float|)| -> |void|:|[/code] when operating 'left' will become: [code]| |(|{|--}) |{|--}|word| |func| |_process|(|delta| : |float|)| -> |void|:|[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

Breaks are set on the edges of contiguous string characters. This includes: [code]"[/code].
For example: [code] "example string" and this: """"""""" [/code] will become: [code]| |"|example| |string|"| |and| |this|: |"|"""""""|"| |[/code] where the [code]|[/code] denotes a break.

No jump behavior.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Single@ |Whitespace| |Double@ |Whitespace|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Single @Whitespace| |Double @Whitespace|[/code]

A single initial whitespace token will be skipped when finding the next caret.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Single@ |Whitespace| |Double@ |Whitespace|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Single| |Whitespace@ |Double| @Whitespace|[/code]

Any initial contiguous whitespace tokens will be skipped when finding the next caret.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Single@ |Whitespace| |Double@ |Whitespace|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Single| |Whitespace@ |Double| |Whitespace@[/code]

Any non-initial trailing contiguous whitespace tokens will be skipped when finding the next caret.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Trailing| @Whitespace| |Example|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Trailing| |Whitespace| @Example|[/code]

A single initial punctuation token will be skipped when finding the next caret. [b]Note:[/b] Requires [constant BREAK_FLAG_SEPARATE_PUNCTUATION] to be set.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Punctuation@ |"|As| @Separate|!|?|"|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Punctuation| @"|As| |Separate@!|?|"|[/code] Move right operation again: [code]|Punctuation| |"@As| |Separate|!@?|"|[/code]

Any initial contiguous punctuation tokens will be skipped when finding the next caret. [b]Note:[/b] Requires [constant BREAK_FLAG_SEPARATE_PUNCTUATION] to be set.
An example with carets denoted with [code]@[/code] and breaks denoted [code]|[/code]: [code]|Punctuation@ |"|As| @Separate|!?"|[/code] Move right operation: [code]|Punctuation| @"|As| |Separate@!?"|[/code] Move right operation again: [code]|Punctuation| |"@As| |Separate|!?"@[/code]
When moving onto the newline, no behavior will happen.
When moving onto a newline, the respective behavior will only happen when the initial token on the newline is a whitespace.
When moving onto a newline, the respective behavior will always happen.
